title: Bisect canonical TensorView entries for coordinate indexing
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView entries are already canonicalized and sorted during construction, but index_coordinate() still used tuple membership and therefore linearly scanned up to the full retained sparse-entry sequence before projecting the coordinate to integer axis positions. The lookup repeated work over an ordering invariant the TensorView already owns.
primary_claim: TensorView.index_coordinate() now reuses the exact canonical entry ordering and bisect_left to locate a retained entry without a full membership scan. Exact retained-entry equality remains the acceptance boundary, so foreign entries still fail closed; source Forest/Fourfold authority, Tensor wire semantics, projection status, provenance and canonical ordering remain unchanged.
gardener_decision: Reuse and centralize the canonical TensorView entry-order key already required by construction, then bisect the immutable ordered tuple. Do not add a label/entry cache, lookup index, service, alternate tensor representation, planner or backend.
acceptance: construction and coordinate indexing use one canonical entry-order definition
index_coordinate locates retained entries with bisect_left over the canonical ordered entry tuple instead of tuple membership
an adversarial 256-entry probe rejects linear membership and bounds integer-index reads to the binary-search shape
a foreign entry with the same coordinate/relation but a different scalar value still fails closed
the Fourfold-v2 workflow executes successfully on the exact code/test revision
the designated Python 3.12/hash-seed-0 Tensor/Forest diagnostic executes successfully
the isolated wheel build/install executes successfully
repository-wide evidence remains collection-only rather than a full-suite execution claim
no OwnerApproval, promotion, Gate transition, measured latency/memory improvement or benchmark superiority claim is created
